artifact_storage.why_it_matters: The hashes above prove a file with this content existed on the machine that ran it. They do not let a reader obtain the recording and replay it, and they cannot be told apart from the hash of a file that no longer exists. Until this is closed, every conclusion here is reproducible by the author alone.

states.available_unverified: a uri exists and nobody outside has checked it
states.independently_verified: another machine downloaded it, verified it, replayed it and left an attestation

cache.note: `sha256_before_seeded` is not restated: the seeded file was replaced in place by the recording. What is checkable now is the source it was seeded from, the entry count before, and the file as it stands.

what_the_run_did.backend_requests_note: logical complete() calls. The provider client is configured with max_retries=5, so the number of HTTP requests may be higher and is not observable from here
what_the_run_did.repeated_attempts_note: all of them cache-served targeted_v4 arm-identity replays, not batch retries. Every batch answered on its first attempt: 7 attempt-0 slots written, 14 retry slots still empty

results.scored_with: --extraction replay --semantic cache-only against the phase7 semantic cache
results.cache_split_note: the global counter is extraction plus semantic. v1 reported the global 16 as the semantic total, which it is not

gate.gate_v1_reason: the gate's state space does not express what happened: MA015: correct -> wrong_but_flagged. Judging it anyway would report a verdict the gate never defined
gate.gate_v1_note: v1 defines `wrong_released` as a wrong value released WITHOUT review, and MA015 carries review_required=True — wrong AND escalated, which v1 has no term for. The FAIL reported on the day was computed by an ad-hoc classifier that contradicted the gate's own text; no executable v1 classifier existed. That FAIL stands as a record of what was reported, not as a verdict v1 ever issued.
gate.gate_v1_second_defect: v1 has no capability floor. Every one of its hard conditions is a prohibition, so a system that refused every row would satisfy all of them and pass.
gate.gate_v2_note: POST-HOC REANALYSIS. v2 was written after this run by an author who knew which verdict it would change; it is published because v1 could not judge the run at all, not because v1's verdict was inconvenient. Its capability floor is deliberately UNSET — a draft set 0.8 and this run keeps exactly 8 of the baseline's 10 correct rows — so the strongest verdict available is PASS (PROHIBITIONS ONLY), which is not a claim that the route works.

reanalyses.status_note: generated BEFORE its own freeze commit, so it carries git_commit '' and status unregistered. It is kept as the development reading that located the defect, and it is NOT release-eligible.
unmet_hard_conditions: hard condition 'wrong_target_accepted_count': the gate requires 0 and the run reports 1 (from metrics.target.gold.identity_wrong_released)
reanalyses.what: The same recording, replayed under aggregation evaluator 1.7.0. Numeric components are verified against each reading's own quote and the survivors carried to the result. No model was asked: backend_requests is 0.
reanalyses.extraction: replay of the D1-7 cache, unchanged
reanalyses.note: MA015 moves from `match` to `mismatch` — the baseline's own verdict — because the source's 99.5% confidence level is now compared against the review's 95%. The components were in the response all along; nothing carried them to the result.
